hints.title: Prefix and Domain Specifications
hints.text: A valid email prefix must start with a letter and contain only alphanumeric characters, underscores, periods, and hyphens.

hints.title: Anchoring Domain Ending
hints.text: The exact domain suffix must be @leetcode.com anchored to the end of the string.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT user_id, name, mail
FROM Users
WHERE mail REGEXP '^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_.-]*@leetcode[.]com$';
```

complexity.notes: Executes regular expression matching across each email string in linear time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Simple string search like contains fails to validate starting character type or illegal special characters.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Regex engine compilation incurs slight constant overhead but guarantees strict pattern compliance.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Regular expression matching anchoring start, character class, and literal dot domain suffix.

solutions.code:
import pandas as pd

def valid_emails(users: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    pattern = r'^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_.-]*@leetcode.com$'
    valid = users['mail'].str.match(pattern).fillna(False)
    return users[valid]
